input: Hi! We're finalizing our wedding reception at a garden estate in Buckhead, Atlanta, a Saturday evening in late April, and still need centerpieces for 15 round tables of 10. Our theme is a water garden, so glass vessels with water as the main element, under about 14 inches so guests can talk across. We'd love something living and moving, not just another flower arrangement, like a little pond on every table, full of life and a real conversation piece, plus a small keepsake guests can take home. Delivery and setup by 3 pm, strike after 11 pm, roughly $1,400–1,950 all in. Could you order the best package for us?

experiences.name: Buckhead Bloom – Classic Southern Low Arrangements
experiences.description: Classic Southern low arrangements for 15 tables: glossy magnolia leaves, white hydrangea and garden roses in gold compotes 8 in tall. Flowers from a Marietta wholesale florist; delivery and setup Saturday 1–3 pm, vessels collected Sunday morning.

experiences.name: Peach & Pond Events – Live Goldfish Bowl Centerpieces
experiences.description: Fifteen glass bowls, each a tiny garden pond with two live goldfish swimming over river pebbles beneath a floating gardenia ring. Each 1-gallon bowl has no filter, aerator or heater; fish arrive the morning of the event and are bagged at strike for guests to take home, and any not taken home are not accepted back by the supplier. Bowls 10 in wide × 8 in tall; gardenias and pebbles from a Marietta wholesale florist; two-person setup crew; tea lights, mirror bases and strike included.

experiences.name: Riverbend Aquascape Co. – Planted Mini-Pond Centerpieces
experiences.description: A low glass tank on each of the 15 tables, planted like a miniature pond with anubias, java fern and floating water lettuce, river stones and hand-blown glass koi suspended mid-water, with a battery-powered bubbler keeping the plants swaying. Aquascapes contain live aquatic plants, stones and glass sculptures only; no fish, snails, shrimp or other live animals. Each guest takes home a mini planted terrarium (150). Tanks 16 × 8 × 8 in; plants from a Decatur nursery greenhouse; glass koi by a Georgia glassblower; Saturday setup crew of three, strike included.

experiences.name: Candle Courtyard Rentals – Votive & Pillar Clusters
experiences.description: Clusters of mercury-glass votives and unscented pillar candles on 12 in square mirror tiles for 15 tables, giving a warm, low glow that keeps sightlines open. Setup and strike included, with an LED option for venues with open-flame limits.

experiences.name: Magnolia Glass Studio – Betta Vase Centerpiece Clusters
experiences.description: Each table gets a cluster of three cylinder vases: one holds a live betta swimming beneath a floating orchid with trailing peace-lily roots, framed by two vases of submerged blooms. The betta's vase is 1 liter, with no heater or filter, and guests take the vase with the fish home as a favor at the end of the night. Clusters 12–14 in tall; orchids from a Gainesville, GA grower; two-person setup crew; chargers, mirror tiles and strike included.

experiences.name: Lotus & Lantern Design – Floating Garden Bowls
experiences.description: Wide glass bowls for all 15 tables, with submerged white orchids, floating gardenias and floating candles that drift across the water. Each guest takes home a small glass water-garden jar with water lettuce and river stones, tagged and ribboned (150 jars). Centerpieces and favors contain plants, flowers, stones and floating candles only; no fish, snails, shrimp or other live animals. Bowls 14 in wide × 6 in tall with a slow water circulator; flowers from a Marietta wholesale florist; Saturday setup by a crew of three, strike included.

experiences.name: Sweet Tea Paper Co. – Reception Table Stationery
experiences.description: Coordinated table stationery for 150 guests: printed table numbers, a menu at each place setting and wildflower seed-paper place cards guests can plant at home. Printed in Atlanta on recycled cotton paper and shipped boxed by table number a week before the wedding.
